name: a-fog-swallowed-park
prompt: A tall portrait illustration made with a steel dip pen and diluted grey ink brushed wet onto brittle, tea-yellowed newsprint, so the paper's own grain and foxing show through the washes. We look down from a little above at a small public garden in 1919, early morning, swallowed by a dense, low, motionless fog. Visibility ends a few strides from the bench: iron railings and the trunks of plane trees are inked crisply at the front, then go faint, then become only pale smudges, then nothing, as if the wash has eaten them. One cast-iron park bench sits dead centre, the only thing drawn with full, hard, black line. On its left end sits a fat rich man in a long dark overcoat and a tall silk top hat, a heavy black mass laid down in dense crosshatching, a shade too large for the bench, which sags under him; the upper part of his hat bleeds softly upward into the grey fog with no edge. His face is half shadow, small pale eyes, a thin satisfied smile, and he lifts one fat gloved hand lazily from the wrist in a bored, dismissive brush-off. At the far right end, small and drawn in thin, broken, faltering line, a young soldier in a worn army greatcoat with one trouser leg pinned up and a wooden crutch beside him, his outline thinning into the mist as if he is already being erased. Flat, sourceless, shadowless dawn light; palette of ink black, three greys of wash and the yellow of old paper, nothing else. Wide empty fog fills the top third of the frame. No lettering, captions, signatures or text anywhere in the picture. Thanks.
